name: Gunung Leuser National Park
blurb: Fig trees, orangutans and tigers in Sumatra's mountain rainforest.

tip.title: Lose the fig trees
tip.text: Figs feed orangutans, hornbills, monkeys and sun bears. Select Fig trees, cut them, and watch the fruit eaters fall, then the tiger.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Gunung Leuser National Park, Sumatran orangutan, Sumatran tiger). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead wood and leaves and return nutrients to the soil.
Figs fruit heavily and feed many forest animals. GloBI records show hornbills, langurs, macaques and bulbuls eating fig fruit near the park.
A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest gaps. GloBI records show langurs, hornbills and doves eating its fruit.
A small forest deer and a documented tiger prey species. It browses plants and fallen fruit.
A large herbivore of the park. GloBI records it eating Prunus arborea, and tigers are recorded preying on elephants.
Wood-eating insects that build mounds in the forest. Sun bears break open their mounds to feed.
A large lizard that eats a range of small animals and carrion. Recorded in the park area by GBIF.

nodes.name: Sumatran tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator, taking deer, pigs, monkeys and other prey. Wikipedia calls the Sumatran population small and fragmented.

story: Gunung Leuser National Park covers 7,927 km² of northern Sumatra, straddling Aceh and North Sumatra. About 40% of it is steep and over 1,500 m high. With two other parks, it forms the Tropical Rainforest Heritage of Sumatra.
matters: It is one of the two remaining habitats of the Sumatran orangutan, which is critically endangered and lives only in northern Sumatra. An orangutan sanctuary operates at Bukit Lawang.
